(Currently Amended) Claim 1: A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, wherein said terminating the flow of air further includes altering a configuration of a control mechanism in fluid communication with the booster device.

(Currently Amended) Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced.

(Currently Amended) Claim 3: The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device while controlling the pressure in said booster device.

(Currently Amended) Claim 4: The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump.

(Currently Amended) Claim 5: The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) Claim 7: The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system, which employs a variable configuration mechanism for controlling vacuum levels.

(Currently Amended) Claim 14: A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to selectively terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, thereby reducing a pressure differential across the pump and parasitic load on the engine.

(Currently Amended) Claim 19: The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system that can adjust its efficiency based on operating parameters.
